target_claim: The explicit crossing schedule in the (<=) direction (initial trip with all of C, K shuttle rounds, then final-stage ferrying of L1 with Charon returning empty) is claimed to be a valid sequence of crossings in which the Charon-free bank always holds an independent set. In fact, during the Final Stage, whenever Charon returns to the left bank to fetch more L1 passengers, the right bank holds the entire cover C unsupervised; if C contains an edge (e.g., H = path a-b-c-d, K=2, minimum cover C={b,c} adjacent), two enemies are left together without Charon, violating the safety condition. The schedule as written is invalid.
source_quote: This procedure produces a valid sequence of crossings using boat capacity k = K + 1. At every point, the bank without Charon holds either an independent set of H’s vertices or is empty.
test_sketch: Implement the schedule generator exactly as written: trip 0 moves C left->right; for i=1..K move C\{ci} right->left then C\{ci} left->right; final stage repeats (Charon returns empty right->left, then carries up to K members of L1 left->right) until L1 is exhausted. Implement a simulator/oracle (~40 lines) that tracks both banks and Charon's position and, after every trip, checks that the bank without Charon induces no edge of H. Input family: small graphs (n <= 12) whose minimum vertex cover contains an edge, simplest H = P4 (edges ab, bc, cd) with K=2, C={b,c}, k=3. The checker flags the first empty return trip of the Final Stage: right bank = {b,c} (enemies, edge bc) with Charon on the left, refuting the quoted claim that the Charon-free bank always holds an independent set. Cross-check with a brute-force BFS over all legal states showing the target configuration is not reached by this schedule legally.
